section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the praises of Rashbi draw his influence (the level of Eitan/Yechidah) into the clarification work of the Tannaim, because the Divine will and delight is specifically in clarification, and this creates the advantage of light from darkness and the two levels of direct and returning light.
section.t: And likewise is the matter regarding the praises of Rashbi,
that through the praises they aroused that his influence be drawn down
(the aspect of Eitan,
Yechidah)
into the study of Torah of the Tannaim, whose study was to clarify clarifications,
this is from the side of the advantage in the matter of clarifications
(over the matter of revelations),
for the will and delight above is specifically in the matter of clarifications.
For this is what is written, "And the Eitanim"
(the letters of Tannaim)
"the foundations of the earth,"
"earth" from the term "will,"
and moreover, "earth" also relates to desire, as it is written,
"You have visited the earth and made it desirous,"
for the will, desire, and delight above is specifically in "earth,"
in the clarification of physical things,
and particularly in the clarification of the matters of damages,
which is done by the "Eitanim, the foundations of the earth."
And through the drawing down of the light of the inner dimension of Torah that is above the matter of clarifications,
the Torah of Rashbi,
to the "Eitanim, the foundations of the earth"
(by which an addition is drawn to them also in the matter of clarifications),
through this an advantage is made in the light,
for the advantage of light comes from
(the clarification of)
darkness.
And moreover, through the drawing down to the "Eitanim, the foundations of the earth"
(the matter of clarifications)
of the influence of Rashbi
(a light that is above the matter of clarifications),
there are two virtues,
the virtue of direct light and the virtue of reflected light,
analogous to "to bring back the righteous in repentance,"
the virtue of the righteous and the virtue of the penitents.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the previous concept to a Zohar story about Rashbi bringing rain through Torah, requiring both his descent and the disciples' arousal, corresponding to the two virtues of the righteous and penitents.
section.t: E)
And one may connect this with the statement of the Zohar,
"Once the world needed rain,
they came before Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Yisa, Rabbi Chizkiyah, and the other comrades,
and through his expounding to them on the verse,
'Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together...' rain fell."
And it is explained in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek
and the Rebbe Maharash,
that although Rashbi drew down the falling of rain through the utterance of Torah in a manner from above to below,
nevertheless, this also required the raising of Mayin Nukvin of the comrades and the praises with which they praised him,
by which they effected an advantage in Rashbi, analogous to "from my students
more than all of them."
And it may be said,
that the connection of this matter to the falling of rain is,
for regarding rain it is written,
"For the Lord God had not caused it to rain... and there was no man to work the ground,"
that the falling of rain is through the work of man,
and particularly through the work of repentance, as our sages said
on the verse,
"May my teaching drop as the rain... when the creatures break their stiff-neckedness, immediately rain falls."
And in the falling of rain through the utterance of Torah of Rashbi
(from above to below)
and the raising of Mayin Nukvin of his disciples
(from below to above)
there were the two virtues,
the virtue of the righteous and the virtue of the penitents.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down of Rashbi's influence (Yechidah) for the sake of clarifications is analogous to the Yechidah of the soul extending into one's four cubits specifically to acquire and refine physical objects.
section.t: And seemingly one may add,
that the drawing down of the influence of Rashbi
(the aspect of Eitan,
Yechidah)
to the "Eitanim, the foundations of the earth" for the sake of the matter of clarifications,
is analogous to what is explained elsewhere
regarding the Yechidah of the soul,
that this that the Yechidah extends into a person's four cubits,
therefore
a person's four cubits acquire for him in any place,
even without his knowledge,
specifically in order to acquire an object placed within them,
the acquisition of a physical thing
(that is external to the person)
into the person's domain,
in order to clarify and refine it by using it for the sake of Heaven,
for the clarification of physical things specifically reaches the Essence.
And likewise is it regarding the Yechidah of Torah
(the Torah of Rashbi),
that it is aroused and drawn down for the sake of the matter of clarifications.
